title: Common-ion effect
examples: Teacher, how does adding salt affect the solubility of other salts?
Could you explain why the common ion effect lowers solubility?
What is the relationship between the common ion and solubility?

explain.say: Today we are looking at the common ion effect in chemistry. This effect predicts solubility changes.
First, let us review the solubility product constant. This constant describes the equilibrium of a sparingly soluble salt.
Next, we consider adding a salt that shares an ion. This added ion is called the common ion. It affects the equilibrium.

draw.text: Adding a common ion shifts equilibrium

explain.say: For example, consider silver chloride dissolving in sodium chloride solution. The added chloride ion is the common ion.
This decrease in solubility is the common ion effect. The added ion pushes the reaction back towards the solid.
In everyday life, this happens when we test for ions. Adding excess chloride can cause silver chloride to precipitate.

faq.q: Does the common ion effect only work for chlorides?
faq.a: No, it applies to any ion present in the solubility equilibrium. You can see this with sulfates or carbonates too.
asks: Does it only work for specific ions?
Can I use this effect with other compounds?

faq.q: Does the common ion effect change the Ksp value?
faq.a: No, the solubility product constant itself remains constant at a given temperature. Only the concentration of dissolved ions changes.
asks: Is Ksp affected by common ions?

faq.q: If I increase the temperature, does that affect the common ion effect?
faq.a: Temperature changes affect the Ksp value, which then changes the solubility. The common ion effect still applies to the new Ksp value.
asks: How does temperature relate to this effect?
Does temperature override the common ion effect?

faq.q: Is it always better to use the common ion effect to predict solubility?
faq.a: It is a very useful tool, but you must first confirm that the salt is sparingly soluble and that the ion is truly common to the equilibrium.
asks: When should I use this concept?
Are there limitations to this prediction?

faq.q: What is the difference between common ion effect and common acid effect?
faq.a: The common ion effect relates to ionic solubility equilibrium. The common acid effect relates to acid-base equilibrium involving weak acids.
asks: What is the difference between these two effects?

facts: The common ion effect predicts a decrease in solubility.
This effect is based on Le Chatelier's principle.
The solubility product constant, Ksp, remains constant.
Adding a common ion shifts the equilibrium left, favoring the solid.

quiz.say: Consider $\text{AgCl}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag}^+(aq) + \text{Cl}^-(aq)$. If we add excess $\text{NaCl}$, what happens to the solubility of $\text{AgCl}$?

options.show: There is no change in solubility
options.say: There is no change in solubility

quiz.why: The added chloride ion acts as a common ion, shifting the equilibrium to the left, thus reducing the amount of dissolved $\text{AgCl}$.

wrong.1: This suggests the added ion pushes the reaction forward, which is incorrect for solubility equilibrium.
wrong.2: This ignores the principle that adding a common ion must affect the equilibrium position.
wrong.3: Ksp is a constant at a given temperature and is not changed by adding a common ion.

quiz.say: If the solubility equilibrium is $\text{BaF}2(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Ba}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{F}^-(aq)$. Adding $\text{NaF}$ will cause:
quiz.why: The added fluoride ion is the common ion, forcing the equilibrium to the left and causing excess solid to form.

wrong.0: The common ion effect deals with ionic concentrations, not necessarily the acidity of the solution.
wrong.1: Increasing solubility would require shifting the equilibrium to the right, which is contrary to the common ion effect.
wrong.2: While concentrations change, the primary observable effect is the precipitation due to the common ion.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes the common ion effect?

options.show: The effect only happens if the salt is weak.
options.say: The effect only happens if the salt is weak.

options.show: The common ion effect only affects the acid strength.
options.say: The common ion effect only affects the acid strength.

options.show: Adding a common ion shifts equilibrium left, decreasing solubility.
options.say: Adding a common ion shifts equilibrium left, decreasing solubility.

options.show: Adding a common ion shifts equilibrium right, increasing solubility.
options.say: Adding a common ion shifts equilibrium right, increasing solubility.

quiz.why: This accurately summarizes the principle: the added ion counteracts the formation of the salt, favoring the solid.

wrong.0: The effect applies to any sparingly soluble salt governed by a Ksp.
wrong.1: Its primary domain is the equilibrium of sparingly soluble ionic compounds.
wrong.3: This describes the opposite effect of what is observed in solubility equilibria.
